text:
Zeev Buium is 20, playing 21 minutes a night on a Canucks blue line that leans on him, and the points have dried up. He has five assists and no goals in 23 games, and only two points in his last ten, while his ice time has climbed past 22 minutes. The Province and The New York Times have both written about how he is handling a season with fewer points than his talent suggests.

Our numbers say part of it is the company. At 5v5 Vancouver gets just 35.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, playing with teammates in the bottom 7% by impact and giving up chances on defense.

The tools that made him the 12th overall pick in 2024 are still visible. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 46% of his entries and shooting off the rush more than most defensemen. Among defensemen drafted near him, the median first full season was 0.24 points a game; he is at 0.22, which is not a slump so much as a normal start.
